title: Prefix catalog: probabilistic merge, session-resilient dedupe, and GPU slot compaction
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Problem: For multi-tenant continuous batching workloads we observe duplicated prefix fragments across requests and sessions that waste GPU-resident KV memory and increase per-token cost. Existing strict exact-key dedupe misses near-duplicates introduced by small prompt edits, slot interpolation, and template parameterization. This ticket designs and implements a session-resilient prefix catalog that enables probabilistic merge of similar prefix fragments, background compaction, and GPU slot compaction to reclaim fragments safely while preserving correctness and latency SLOs.

Goals:
- Increase GPU KV hit rate for real workloads by reusing near-duplicate prefixes across sessions and tenants where allowed by isolation policies.
- Reduce resident GPU KV footprint through compaction and slab packing without increasing tail latency beyond SLO.
- Provide controlled probabilistic merging (merge hooks) with tunable similarity thresholds and safety checks so we avoid hallucinated cache reuse.

High-level approach:
1) Prefix fingerprinting: compute a dual-hash fingerprint (fast 64-bit rolling + locality-sensitive hash) for each prefix fragment at insertion time. Store both in the catalog index entry.
2) Probabilistic candidate selection: use a small LSH table keyed by the locality-sensitive sketch to return merge candidates cheaply. Use an additional Bloom filter per tenant to avoid cross-tenant leakage for isolation-sensitive configs.
3) Merge decision: run a lightweight similarity comparator on CPU (token overlap, n-gram Jaccard, and dot-product on a compact prefix embedding) to accept or reject merge. Record merge provenance metadata (merged_from keys delimited) to enable rollback during evictions.
4) Atomic GPU compaction: when multiple fragments are merged, create a new compacted slab on GPU with coalesced KV entries; install via an atomic pointer swap and mark old slabs for asynchronous reclamation.
5) Slot packing heuristic: use a best-fit bin packing of fragment sizes per GPU slab to minimize wasted slots; prefer moving small merged fragments into existing underutilized slabs before allocating new ones.
6) Background compaction worker: async compaction that throttles to avoid extra tail latency. Compaction is scheduled based on fragmentation ratio and memory pressure signals from the allocator.

Trade-offs considered:
- False merges vs memory savings: Conservative similarity thresholds reduce incorrect reuse but reduce savings. We will expose threshold knobs: conservative, balanced, aggressive.
- CPU cost of similarity checks: offloading heavy checks to CPU can increase host overhead; we limit checks by LSH prefilter and sample-based acceptance.
- Multi-tenant safety: default behavior is tenant-isolated dedupe. Allow cross-tenant merge only if the tenant ACL and contract permit shared fragments (Dedicated customers can opt-in).

Instrumentation and metrics (initial):
- prefix_merge_rate: fraction of insertions that were merged (by threshold bucket).
- prefix_hit_delta: change in KV hit rate attributable to merged entries (requires trace-level attribution).
- slab_fragmentation_ratio: fraction of slab bytes unused due to internal fragmentation.
- compaction_duration_ms: histogram of compaction job runtime.
- rollback_rate: fraction of merges that were later rolled back due to correctness/regression signals.
- tail_p99_increase_ms: p99 latency delta when compaction concurrent with serving.

Design/implementation phases:
- Phase 1 (spike): implement dual-fingerprint and LSH prefilter on CPU, simulate merge decisions offline using 2 weeks of sampled production traces. Deliver a Confluence doc with measured collision rates and memory/reuse projections. (Spike complete: link below)
- Phase 2 (PoC): implement in-memory catalog + merge logic in the runtime, but use host-side compacted storage (not yet GPU-resident). Validate correctness and benchmarks.
- Phase 3 (GPU integration): implement atomic slab compaction and slot packing in GPU allocator; add async reclamation and safe rollback.
- Phase 4 (opt-in rollout): expose controls in the Console and enable opt-in for non-sensitive tenants; run canary with traffic shaping and mitigate regressions.

Links:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/PKV-Session-Resilient-Prefix-Catalog
- Spike results notebook (internal): drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XxExampleSpikeNotebook
- GitHub spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1857

Implementation notes:
- Fingerprinting uses fnv64_xor for quick equality buckets and a 128-bit SimHash compressed to 64 bits for similarity LSH. We keep a short token sketch (first/last n tokens) to catch template parameter shifts.
- Catalog index stored as a compact vector of entries: key, fnv64, simhash64, size_bytes, tenant_id, last_used_ts, merged_from_list (comma-separated ids). All values stored in host memory index; heavy payload remains in GPU slabs.
- To avoid long GC pauses, evicted/old slabs are enqueued for batched free that runs outside request path. Reclamation also triggers compaction when fragmentation ratio > 30%.
- Rollback: when a merged entry is found to cause a quality regression (via evals or output divergence), we record rollback cause and perform an atomic unmerge: re-create previous slabs from provenance pointers if still available or mark the merged entry as no-merge for a TTL.

Security & privacy:
- Cross-tenant merge is disabled by default. For Dedicated/Private customers we honor KSIs and contractual restrictions.
- Bloom filters per-tenant ensure quick exclusion of tenants from candidate pools.
- Merged provenance metadata is treated as internal debug data and access-controlled.

Risks and mitigations:
- Incorrect merge causing subtle output differences: mitigate with canaries, A/B evals on representative prompts, and quick rollback hooks.
- GPU compaction impacting p99 latency: throttle compaction and prefer off-peak windows; instrument and auto-disable compaction if p99 regresses > configured threshold.
- State explosion in merged_from metadata: cap provenance length and use sampling/summary when provenance gets too long.

Next steps / immediate todos:
- Marco: land LSH index and dual fingerprint computation in runtime core (WIP branch: feature/prefix-catalog).
- Aisha: add Confluence section with similarity thresholds and tuned knobs for POC.
- QA: prepare prompt regression set and load test harness for canary (estimate 3 days).
- Infra: allocate 2 dev GPUs with tracing flags enabled for compaction telemetry.

Estimated savings (simulation):
- Median-case: 10-18% reduction in GPU KV resident bytes for sampled customer workloads.
- Best-case (templated SaaS traffic): up to 35% reduction.
- Expected CPU overhead: +3-6% host cycles on average for insertion-heavy workloads with balanced threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog computes two fingerprints for each prefix insertion and populates LSH index.
Offline simulation demonstrates measurable reuse (>8% GPU KV reduction) on sampled traces with conservative threshold.
PoC running in runtime can merge and unmerge in host memory without impacting p99 by >5% during test harness runs.
GPU compaction path implemented and can atomically swap compacted slabs for merged entries in a controlled dev canary.
Console has a toggle (off/conservative/balanced/aggressive) and an opt-in flag per tenant for cross-tenant merge.
Monitoring dashboards show prefix_merge_rate, slab_fragmentation_ratio, compaction_duration_ms, rollback_rate.
